RT Michael Pettis
FT: In Brazil, "almost 2mn people, mostly men, now work full-time for transport or delivery apps — around 2 per cent of the workforce — with driver numbers climbing 37 per cent in three years, according to government research. The most common reason people work for the apps is that they could not find another job."

items.title: NYT: "Surging exports and the industrial production needed to sustain them kept China’s economy growing over the past three months, even as consumer ...
items.description_html:
NYT: "Surging exports and the industrial production needed to sustain them kept China’s economy growing over the past three months, even as consumer spending stagnated and investment plunged. The result is an economy increasingly dependent on selling goods abroad, even as domestic demand deteriorates."

NYT's Keith Bradsher gets this right. Many other analysts have been presenting this year's economic data as describing a two-track economy, with a sluggish domestic economy being balanced by a brilliant export economy.

But that is a very poor description of what is actually happening. Yes, net exports are surging, but this isn't a sign of a viable export sector. If the export sector were very profitable, it might make sense to describe it this way, but exports aren't especially profitable except in relation to domestic sales, where except in a few sectors businesses are struggling to make any profit at all, and once direct and indirect subsidies are backed out, much of China's exports are net value destroyers for the economy, with the losses capitalized on balance sheets in the form of surging debt.

When an economy produces far more than it can absorb through domestic consumption or investment, it must either export the balance or close down domestic production. Given how high real unemployment is, especially among the young, Beijing has no choice but to force the former, even if this comes at an economic cost.

The surge in China's net exports, in other words, is not a sigh of a strong and profitable export sector. If it takes rising debt, continued subsidies, and growing exports in order to prevent a contraction in domestic production, the surge in net exports is simply another way of describing weak domestic demand.

Surging exports are usually a good sign for an economy. Surging net exports usually are not.
https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/18/business/china-economy-gdp.html?smid=tw-share

items.title: None of the data that came out today gives us a different picture of the Chinese economy from what we’ve seen all year. The economy is still heavily ...
items.description_html:
None of the data that came out today gives us a different picture of the Chinese economy from what we’ve seen all year. The economy is still heavily focused on boosting production and is still struggling with boosting demand.

GDP grew 4.5% year on year in the third quarter of 2026, slightly higher than expected, from 5.0% in the first quarter and 4.3% in the second quarter. Year to date GDP has grown 4.6%, just above the bottom of the GDP growth target for 2026.

In September, industrial output went up by 5.5% year on year, or 5.3% for the first nine months. Meanwhile retail sales increased by 1.1% in September, or 2.6% for the first nine months.

The gap between domestic production and domestic consumption, in other words, continues to widen rather than narrow, with the gap much wider in September than it has been over the rest of the year. This can only be balanced by rising investment or a rising trade surplus.

And it clearly isn’t being balanced by rising investment. Fixed asset investment in the first nine months of 2026 was down 7.2% year on year, or 4.2% with property investment deducted.

The decline in overall investment was driven by an even sharper decline in private investment, which was down by 10.4% year on year, or 6.7% with property investment deducted. Disaggregated by sector, investment in infrastructure declined by 4.2% year on year, manufacturing by 2.1%, and real estate development by 20.6%. The good news is that the decline in investment may finally be bottoming out, with fixed asset investment in September, rising by 0.07% month on month.

We will probably see fiscal expansion in the last quarter of this year, although I think it would be a good thing if Beijing let growth come in at the bottom of the target, especially if they lower the target further in 2027. Debt is simply growing too fast, and it is growing fast only because of the urgent desire to meet politically-determined GDP growth targets. The longer this goes on, the more difficult the ultimate adjustment will be.
https://english.news.cn/20261019/2da9b2afcdaf42d3a3f009c338edd92a/c.html

items.title: RT Roger E. A. Farmer: That’s a question for the philosophy of science. My friend Axel Leijonhufvud had a metaphor of science as a tree with many bra...
items.description_html:
RT Roger E. A. Farmer
That’s a question for the philosophy of science. My friend Axel Leijonhufvud had a metaphor of science as a tree with many branches. Each branch represents an alternative possible path along which the subject might progress.

In the experimental sciences, false approaches are quickly discovered by experiment and those branches are trimmed. Progress appears linear.

In non experimental sciences the discipline can adopt approaches that are ultimately shown to be false but which persist for long periods of time. Ultimately it takes a large natural experiment like the Great Depression or the Stagflation of the 1970s to cause a course correction.

In the period between natural experiments, when multiple theories appear equally viable, the science is governed by gatekeepers who edit top journals and are educated at a small group of elite institutions. These gatekeepers provide a filter on acceptable discourse. This institutional structure has its benefits since, if it is difficult to empirically distinguish alternative theories, it would be highly disruptive if every fresh graduate student were to branch out in an entirely new direction. But the filtering out of new ideas can also cause the exiting corpus of thought to become sclerotic.

Influential schools of thought, like NK economics, are practiced by generations of students who acquire human capital and have an incentive not to rock the boat. Prestigious awards like the Nobel Prize and the John Bates Clarke Award provide incentives to color within the lines and these incentives are strongest when widely recognized deserving recipients have not yet been recognized. Elite universities maintain active offices whose goal is to lobby the Nobel committee on behalf of their own professoriate.

I have never met a brilliant young academic who did not aspire to be recognized as a Nobel Laureate: Through that mechanism prestigious awards offer important incentives to scientific excellence. But the prizes themselves also act as brakes on progress since a major course correction in the direction of the discipline would depreciate, overnight, the accumulated capital of generations of scholars.

In the words of Max Planck: “Progress occurs one funeral at a time.”

For further reading on these ideas I recommend Lakatos’ essay in in ‘Criticism and the Growth of Knowledge’ https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/criticism-and-the-growth-of-knowledge/74C4E5A7D52C5D11F65849CCD0710012

items.title: RT Press Trust of India: VIDEO | Delhi: Reacting to the judicial custody of CJP co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, CJP legal head Ratna Singh...
items.description_html:
RT Press Trust of India
VIDEO | Delhi: Reacting to the judicial custody of CJP co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, CJP legal head Ratna Singh says, "We have been here since morning. We were told that the entire hearing would take place at 12.00 pm. Today, everything was complete, the verification was done, and all requirements were met. We have been waiting here since noon. The SEM (Special Executive Magistrate) was at the police station by 1:30 pm, but he did not enter the courtroom until 5.00 pm. When he finally arrived, he refused to hear our case on its merits regarding whether Saurav and Ashutosh should be released from judicial custody. Instead, he made arbitrary remarks. The public prosecutor, who had not appeared at the police station for the last four days, was present today. Within about five minutes of the proceedings, the SEM told the court that he had received a threatening message. From that point on, the entire discussion revolved solely around that message. It is clear that this entire episode was orchestrated. They had decided beforehand to come into the courtroom and focus exclusively on this alleged threatening message, completely bypassing whether the formalities required for Saurav and Ashutosh's release were fulfilled. Given how this process has been deliberately delayed and handled, I am utterly disappointed..."

(Full video available on PTI Videos - http://ptivideos.com)

items.title: RT Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський: We don’t use Starlink for our responses inside Russia. We use Starlink to intercept...
items.description_html:
RT Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський
We don’t use Starlink for our responses inside Russia. We use Starlink to intercept jet-powered “shaheds” that attack our civilians and kill families.

Starlink wasn’t turned off – its speed was reduced. And when the speed was reduced, we were unable to intercept a certain number of jet-powered “shaheds.” We couldn’t use a tool that helps protect people. That’s very painful and frustrating.

We also use Starlink for mid-range strikes against enemy military targets in our temporarily occupied territories. We couldn’t do that when the restrictions were in place. And third, what matters most is people. Our warriors, who spend weeks and months on the front line, receive food and water delivered by drones using Starlink.

Has the speed been fully restored to what it was before? No. Is it being restored now? Yes.

From a conversation with media representatives in Brussels. (2/3)

items.title: RT Intrinsic Compounding: Engineered Goods exports from India India’s engineering exports grew 20% in H1 FY27 to $70.9 bn. EEPC now expects a record ...
items.description_html:
RT Intrinsic Compounding
Engineered Goods exports from India

India’s engineering exports grew 20% in H1 FY27 to $70.9 bn. EEPC now expects a record $150 bn this year.

Why the sudden jump? 5 reasons:

1. Metals boom. The Iran war shut the Strait of Hormuz and knocked out Gulf aluminium, about 8% of world supply. Prices hit a 4-year high. India’s aluminium exports jumped 49% in May, and steel exports 51% in July.

2. US tariff reset. Washington cut tariffs on Indian goods from 50% to 18% in February. Shipments to the US were up 20% in July.

3. China is buying. Engineering exports to China rose 82% in April and 74% in June.

4. A new door into West Asia. With routes to the UAE and Saudi blocked, exports to Oman more than quadrupled in June.

5. The UK trade deal is live. It kicked in on 15 July, and UK shipments were already up 34% in the first two months of the year.

Engineered Goods exports from India

India’s engineering exports grew 20% in H1 FY27 to $70.9 bn. EEPC now expects a record $150 bn this year.

Why the sudden jump? 5 reasons:

1. Metals boom. The Iran war shut the Strait of Hormuz and knocked out Gulf aluminium, about 8% of world supply. Prices hit a 4-year high. India’s aluminium exports jumped 49% in May, and steel exports 51% in July.

2. US tariff reset. Washington cut tariffs on Indian goods from 50% to 18% in February. Shipments to the US were up 20% in July.

3. China is buying. Engineering exports to China rose 82% in April and 74% in June.

4. A new door into West Asia. With routes to the UAE and Saudi blocked, exports to Oman more than quadrupled in June.

5. The UK trade deal is live. It kicked in on 15 July, and UK shipments were already up 34% in the first two months of the year.

Freeze dried coffee demand in the world remains much hihger than Spray Dried as per CCL Product's concall @stockscansin

Freeze-dried coffee and spray-dried coffee are both forms of instant coffee, but they use completely different methods to remove water from liquid coffee extract.

How They Are Made

Freeze-Dried Coffee: The coffee extract is frozen solid at very low temperatures and then placed in a vacuum chamber. Through a process called sublimation, the ice turns directly into vapor without melting into liquid. This gentle, low-temperature method leaves behind large, porous, crystalline granules.

Spray-Dried Coffee: Liquid coffee concentrate is sprayed in a fine mist through hot air inside a large, sealed tower. The heat causes the water to evaporate almost instantly, leaving behind a fine, uniform powder.

Freeze dried coffee is more expensive as it ends up retaining the aroma and richness of the coffee. Spray Dried is commonly used as a low cost instant coffee which is easily dissovable.

2 Indian Manufacturers of them same are:

1. CCL Products (India) Ltd.

CCL Products is the world's largest private-label instant coffee manufacturer with a total aggregate capacity of 77,000 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA) across facilities in India and Vietnam. Within that, their freeze-dried coffee footprint stands at 17,000 MTPA.

2. Vintage Coffee and Beverages Ltd

Current Installed Capacity: The company currently operates at an installed capacity of 11,000 MTPA.

Upcoming Freeze-Dried Expansion: Vintage Coffee signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Telangana government to build a standalone, state-of-the-art premium freeze-dried coffee manufacturing facility with a capacity of 5500 MTPA.

items.title: RT Nandakishor m: Around 3 weeks ago introduced Laya, the first open-source version of JEV, and it has reached a very large scale. Today I am open-sou...
items.description_html:
RT Nandakishor m
Around 3 weeks ago introduced Laya, the first open-source version of JEV, and it has reached a very large scale. Today I am open-sourcing a new physics-based typed decision model called Vega.
The interesting parts. It is only 800 million parameters (4B is also there), with 73k token support, image support, and surpassing many of the jev benchmarks in single-shot. Implemented an engine+adapter as a Test-Time Training Architecture.
Imagine you are giving input to the model like "ignore all previous conversations," which is called the observation, along with a question, "Is this trying to override the instructions of the model?" and your possible outcomes are YES or NO. The whole prompt is passed to an LLM/VLM (yeah, image-supported), then from the hidden layers, we can extract the observation, question, the yes and no, and last token. These will be vectors, and we can project it by multiplying with wieghts; then, first, using the observation projection, we can create a landscape with valleys; then, using the question and last-token vectors, we can initialise a ball in the valley, and using YES or NO, we can get the candidate location of the ball. Depends on the number of outcomes we create valleys; that is, here YES and NO, so 2. When the ball fall on YES valley, we get the answer. There is friction also influencing how the ball moves.
TLDR: It's like creating valleys of outcomes that we need and throwing a ball that will slow down based on friction and settle on the best outcome

items.description_html:
RT Prasanna Tantri
To appreciate the Indian government’s caution on Starlink, I strongly recommend Edward Fishman’s New York Times bestseller, Chokepoints. It shows how America turned its dominance in finance and technology into instruments of state policy.

Private ownership offers no insulation from state power. The restrictions on Huawei and ZTE illustrate how dependence on American technology can become a source of geopolitical vulnerability. Under the Foreign Direct Product Rule, even companies outside America needed US permission to supply Huawei with certain products made using American technology. Washington’s reach extended far beyond American firms and borders.

India should take that lesson seriously. Greater dependence on foreign-controlled critical infrastructure creates the risk that commercial access will eventually become conditional on political compliance.

Economic interdependence can deliver prosperity. But in periods of geopolitical conflict, it can also constrain a country’s freedom to make its own choices. Short-term commercial gains must be weighed against that loss of autonomy.

India is right to insist on security safeguards for Starlink. Economic sovereignty is difficult to recover once critical dependencies are entrenched.

For most, non-tech, investors, AI equates to AI infra. And that's only 50% of the story which has already played out. It's blowoff top euphoric phase we're in. The reasoning is on the way to getting commodatized. For in infra player, cost are insanely high & capex is forever. What they sell out in market *was* getting premium. It's temporal. The time to be bullish on infra was late 2023, early 2024.

When people say AI is in bubble, it's the infra players & their stock prices not the rest of the part of the value chain.

In the last two decades, we saw similar cycles playing out with specialized server builders. The value went out and accrued in software.

There are two way forward. For an LLM OEM, raising prices will not work. The only other way is build around the reasoning. Build tools, harness, something valuable that keeps enterprises spending. There is no clear path to profitability for these LLM players & the IPOs are looking to suck everything out. The value will once again move out and get into data, harness, security, the non infra part. With non programmers vibe coding & putting millions of lines of code, agents into production, diff set of value pockets attracts premium. The infra players who build tools for observability, auditability, monitoring, governance will still stay very relevant.

I read it long ago that in market cycles, themes pick up & initially few believe in it. Eventually, everyone starts believing in it. In my view with infra, we're in this phase. Demand won't go down, but premium won't be same. The early investors of infra have moved deep within value chain, away from infra if you track deals globally. Then the open weight models, onchip inference and so much architectural advancements awaiting in line. The transition will be much faster, if not instant.

items.title: Why could cybersecurity become a megatrend? Most security has been built around one assumption: the danger comes from someone who wants to cause harm....
items.description_html:
Why could cybersecurity become a megatrend?

Most security has been built around one assumption: the danger comes from someone who wants to cause harm. A hacker, a scammer, a disgruntled employee. So we build walls, filters and permissions to keep bad intentions out.

That assumption may be becoming outdated. The bigger danger with AI agents may not be an agent that wants to cause harm, but one that is too determined to do exactly what it was told.

Consider this as an example: agents were given a legitimate task: complete a cybersecurity test. When the obvious route was blocked, they found another way. They escaped their sandbox, retrieved passwords and gained access they were not supposed to have. Nobody told them to attack anything. They were simply doing their job and did not care how they got it done.

Think of telling a friend: “Get me a coffee, whatever it takes.” A normal person understands the implicit boundaries. “Whatever it takes” does not mean robbing the café. An AI agent may not automatically understand those boundaries. It isn't evil. It is obedient without necessarily possessing common sense about where the objective should stop.

This is where the tail risk becomes interesting. We tend to prepare for risks based on what we expect an adversary to do. But a sufficiently capable system can create a serious problem without any malicious intent at all. It only needs a strong objective, enough capability and insufficient constraints.

And AI agents dramatically increase the number of entities that can act inside a digital environment. More agents, more autonomy, more permissions, more connections and more opportunities for unintended behaviour.

The attack surface is no longer just humans trying to break into systems. It increasingly includes machines acting inside them.

We were guarding the door against the burglar. The unexpected risk may come from the helper we willingly let inside.

And perhaps the most uncomfortable thought is this:

The dangerous AI agent may not be the one that refuses to follow instructions. It may be the one that follows them perfectly.

items.description_html:
One of the most useful ideas in Taleb's Antifragile is the forest-fire analogy.

Suppress small fires for long enough and dead wood accumulates. Eventually, when a fire comes, there is simply too much fuel.

Markets can work the same way.

Small, periodic corrections can be the financial equivalent of controlled burns. They expose leverage, reset expectations, flush out weak hands and force investors to reassess risk.

That is why I actually think it is healthy that the AI-related theme in the US market is correcting periodically and, so far, relatively orderly.

The alternative is not "no correction".

The alternative may be a much larger correction later, when far more capital, leverage and expectations have accumulated around the same narrative.

And by then, the damage won't be confined to professional investors.

It will reach millions of retirement accounts and 401(k)s.

A small fire today may be painful. A forest fire later can be devastating.

That is the Talebian lesson: sometimes what looks like instability is precisely what prevents systemic fragility.

Two numbers stood out:

AI solutions in biopharma: 42–45% CAGR through 2030. Frontier AI capability: doubling every 5.2 months.

The interesting part isn’t the AI growth itself.

If discovery gets dramatically faster, the bottleneck eventually moves downstream.

More molecules entering the clinic means more demand for development, scale-up and commercial manufacturing capacity.

AI may accelerate the molecule.

The physical world still has to make it.

items.title: RT Swapnil Srivastav: 🚨 Indian logistics companies have found the perfect scam: steal from D2C brands and let the customer take the blame. Here’s ...
items.description_html:
RT Swapnil Srivastav
🚨 Indian logistics companies have found the perfect scam: steal from D2C brands and let the customer take the blame.

Here’s how it works:

→ Prepaid order gets “cancelled” without the customer or brand knowing

→ Brand gets charged two-way delivery fees for an order nobody cancelled

→ Small items get shipped back in oversized boxes to inflate the RTO cost

→ Customer calls in confused: “I never cancelled this, I was waiting for it”

The brand loses the product, the shipping cost, the RTO cost, and the customer relationship. In one transaction.

Every D2C founder in India has lived this. Not once. On repeat.

And the wildest part? This is a multi thousand crore leak across the industry and almost nobody is building to fix it. 🤷🏻‍♂️

items.title: P/B ratio has historically been a more reliable and stable valuation metric for predicting future returns compared to alternatives such as P/E or EV/E...
items.description_html:
P/B ratio has historically been a more reliable and stable valuation metric for predicting future returns compared to alternatives such as P/E or EV/EBITDA. I had demonstrated this through correlation analysis in an earlier investor memo.

The chart below tracks the P/B ratio (blue line) of the Nifty Smallcap 100 Index against the 25th percentile of its trailing 5-year P/B range (orange line). In simple terms, when the blue line falls below the orange line, the current valuation is in the lowest quartile of the past five years.

Since P/B is broadly proportional to ROE, the structural improvement in index ROE—from ~8–12% in the previous decade to ~15% currently—has led to a gradual upward shift in the orange line over time.

Notably, for the first time since the COVID crash, the current P/B has moved below this 25th percentile threshold. Historically, similar instances—during the 2011–2013 downturn, Q1 2016 correction, and the COVID crash—have been followed by strong returns over the subsequent 1–3 years.

This does not imply that markets have bottomed, nor does it guarantee short-term gains. In an event-driven environment, especially with geopolitical risks such as an escalation in war, markets could decline further by 10–20%.

However, what can be said with a reasonably high degree of confidence is that forward-looking returns over a 1–3 year horizon from such valuation levels have historically been better than average.

items.title: In my experience, this is probably the first time the Mid & Small cap indices have outperformed the Nifty 50 during a crisis time. It's also extremely...
items.description_html: In my experience, this is probably the first time the Mid & Small cap indices have outperformed the Nifty 50 during a crisis time. It's also extremely rare to see the Mid & Small cap indices (avg of the two) beating the Nifty 50 near the bottom of the cycle. Their avg CAGR has outperformed during the last two tough years as well as all the below trailing years. I am not that surprised as their balance sheet, P&L and cash flow quality has substantially improved post COVID. I believe the biggest multi-baggers will emerge from this space as the earnings growth differential will be significant going forward. Because of the quality differential today vs during pre-COVID period, I would be surprised if their valuations correct to levels seen during the previous crashes. We probably have the best corporate quality and least stressed financials currently compared to any other previous big crisis.

items.description_html:
RT Javier Blas
MIDDLE EAST FLOWS: Not only flows have proven resilient, but over the last few days (particularly since Oct 16), SoH traffic has surged despite Iranian attacks.

Total Middle East crude flows (ex-Iran, including SoH and all the bypass pipelines and routes) are back to >90% of pre-war levels (last seen in late Sept), and even higher if using a short 7-day average. Refined products flows remain significantly below. Caveat: flows are very uneven, with some days of large number of tanker crossings, followed by very quiet days.

Overall, physical Middle East crude oil premia has continued to drop; just the opposite of what has happened to flat prices. The Oman-Dubai differential has fallen to a 3-month low of ~$4 a barrel. The differential was >$30 a barrel in mid-Sept.


Javier Blas: MIDDLE EAST OIL FLOWS: Despite a wave of Iranian attacks since the beginning of October, total Middle Eastern crude oil flows (ex-Iran) remain resilient. Flows are becoming, however, lumpier (days of multiple tanker crossings followed by days of very few tankers).

The report stated that before Jio's 4G launch, India had only 2 Unicorns. 2021, there were 37 unicorns, and it had forecasted 100 Unicorns in 2025. That came true, and we did even better. items.title: RT Rahul Ajmera: What if you could see every new housing project in Pune on one page, with its construction progress, what flats actually sold for, an...
items.description_html:
RT Rahul Ajmera
What if you could see every new housing project in Pune on one page, with its construction progress, what flats actually sold for, and the price per sqft, without giving anyone your phone number?

Today, one search puts your phone number in ten hands. Listings are paid for. Prices are “on request”. And the real records are nearly impossible for an ordinary buyer to use.

So Stratig Consulting and I have built http://FlatNama.com, a free, independent guide to new projects across Pune & PCMC.

What it shows:
→ Every project drawn as a building, showing how much is actually built (as reported to MahaRERA)
→ Registered possession dates, and whether they’ve been extended
→ Units booked so far
→ Each project compared with others in its PIN code
→ Actual registered sale prices and price per sqft from Department of Registration and Stamps, Government of Maharashtra

What it doesn’t have: Ads, Paid listings, Sign-ups, or a Request for your phone number.

As far as we know, no other website puts real sale prices next to construction progress, free, on one page.

An honest note: http://FlatNama.com is live and being updated regularly. Prices & Construction Updates are rolling out area by area, and within about a month we hope to cover the most popular areas and prominent projects in Pune.

How can we improve this website? Tell me in the comments.

items.title: RT Aabhas Maldahiyar 🇮🇳: On the auspicious occasion of Durga Puja, I wrote this piece for @IndiaToday (Link https://www.indiatoday.in/opinion/st...
items.description_html:
RT Aabhas Maldahiyar 🇮🇳
On the auspicious occasion of Durga Puja, I wrote this piece for @IndiaToday (Link https://www.indiatoday.in/opinion/story/shivaji-maharana-pratap-dussehra-goddess-bhawani-shakti-sword-maratha-worship-warrior-traditions-3020051-2026-10-19 ) I explore a forgotten force behind India’s warrior traditions: the Mother Goddess, the sword, and the sacred idea of resistance.

Why did Rajput warriors invoke Shakti? Why did Bhawani hold such a powerful place in the memory of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj? And what does Dussehra reveal about a civilisation that saw devotion as a source of courage?

From Maharana Pratap’s defiance to Shivaji Maharaj’s struggle for Swarajya, the Rajputs and Marathas forged legacies in which faith, honour and the will to fight stood intertwined.

The sword was steel. The cause was sovereignty. And for these warriors, the Goddess was no distant abstraction confined to a shrine.

Centuries later, revolutionaries would invoke the Mother as Shakti in their battle against British rule.

Dussehra celebrates victory. But who remembers the faith that sent warriors into battle when victory was far from certain?

This is the martial soul of Navaratri: not merely worshipping the Divine Mother, but drawing from Shakti the courage to resist, endure and fight.

items.title: RT Kyle Chan: India might be the focus of China's new export controls on construction machinery. India is not called out explicitly, but China is now ...
items.description_html:
RT Kyle Chan
India might be the focus of China's new export controls on construction machinery.

India is not called out explicitly, but China is now prohibiting certain machinery to "sensitive countries and regions that have disputes with China" 与中国存在争议的敏感国家和地区.

These include:
- Tunnel-boring machines, which China has appeared to limit to India in the past
- High-altitude concrete spraying machines (above 3,000 m altitude), which might be about military construction in the Himalayas


Kyle Chan: China is rolling out even more export controls.

Just days after draft export controls on AI, biotech, and solar, China is now adding or updating export controls on dual-use items:
- Drones
- Construction machinery
- Dredging equipment

items.title: RT Sustainable Futures Collaborative: As India advances towards the more ambitious and hard-to-attain 500 GW non-fossil domestic target by 2030, the c...
items.description_html:
RT Sustainable Futures Collaborative
As India advances towards the more ambitious and hard-to-attain 500 GW non-fossil domestic target by 2030, the central challenge is no longer merely the scale of non-fossil capacity deployment. Rather, it lies in ensuring that this capacity is effectively integrated into the power system and translated into actual clean electricity generation that delivers broad socioeconomic benefits. In other words, capacity deployment should simultaneously pave the way for system integration and socioeconomic transformation.

In @Ideas4India, @SaradaPD and Shubhranshu Suman explain why we need to think beyond capacity addition amid a growing and increasingly volatile electricity demand. They argue that policy attention must shift towards increasing the share of electricity generated from non-fossil sources, better integrating renewables into the grid, and fostering productive use of power that can generate livelihood opportunities.

items.title: RT For Our Futures: University of Chicago Students to Protest at Chicago Mercantile Exchange, Demand End to Federal Ban on Onion Futures Student-led g...
items.description_html:
RT For Our Futures
University of Chicago Students to Protest at Chicago Mercantile Exchange, Demand End to Federal Ban on Onion Futures
Student-led group For Our Futures will rally Monday morning to call for repeal of the 1958 Onion Futures Act

On Monday, October 19, at 8:30 a.m., members of For Our Futures, a student-led organization from @UChicago, will gather outside the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (@CMEGroup) headquarters to demand the repeal of the Onion Futures Act of 1958, a nearly 70-year-old federal law prohibiting futures trading in onions.

The Onion Futures Act, enacted following allegations of market manipulation in the 1950s, singled out onions for a prohibition on futures contracts that remains in effect today. For Our Futures is calling on Congress to repeal the ban and restore the ability of onion growers, buyers, and traders to participate in a regulated futures market. Onions remain the only commodity banned from futures trading in the United States.

The protest will feature a giant inflatable onion costume, protest signs, and dozens of students, and will take place outside the headquarters of CME Group, one of the world's largest derivatives marketplaces and the historic center of American onion futures trading.

DM for details

RT Nithin Kamath
The ED just froze trading accounts holding about ₹200 crore in an alleged WhatsApp-driven pump and dump involving two listed companies.

It's crazy that even in 2026, people still fall for stock tips on WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, and social media. This is probably the silliest way to lose money.

Given how late in the cycle we are, these instances are only going to increase. We're already seeing more pump and dumps, whether through WhatsApp groups or influencers peddling IPOs and stocks. This won't end well.

So the next time you get a message promising easy money, just ask Claude or ChatGPT whether it's a good idea. It could save you a lot of money.

It's become a cliché, but nowhere is "if it's too good to be true, it probably is" truer than in the stock market.

items.title: RT Prasanna Viswanathan: China announces export controls for tunnel boring machines (TBMs) From Nov 18, exporting TBMs will require a licence. These a...
items.description_html:
RT Prasanna Viswanathan
China announces export controls for tunnel boring machines (TBMs)

From Nov 18, exporting TBMs will require a licence. These are the machines fuelling India’s infrastructurebooming especially metros and highway tunnels.

Beijing is classifying them as “dual-use” items, which gives the move a security label, but in effect it is economic coercion.

This has happened before. In 2024, China began delaying customs clearances for TBM shipments to India, and in August 2025 it told India it had lifted the curbs on TBMs. With this licence rule, the delays become a formal mechanism that Beijing can tighten or loosen whenever relations change.

India’s dependence here is real, but it is narrower than it might look. TBM imports from China had already dropped sharply, from $18 million in 2022-23 to $3 million in 2023-24, and most self-propelled TBMs have come from outside China. The serious risk is deayed metro timelines and cost escalation if suppliers’ Chinese plants or components get stuck in licensing.

India’s response has to be to make these machines itself, and that work has started. The government is preparing a $1.2 billion incentive scheme to make tunnel boring machines, firefighting equipment and elevators in India. It is expected to bring in about $1.8 billion in investment over seven years.

BEML is preparing to manufacture TBMs locally, and L&T could also benefit. Building this capacity will take years, but each round of export controls from China makes the case for it stronger. https://asia.nikkei.com/economy/china-announces-export-controls-for-tunnel-boring-machines

items.title: Interesting proposal. I believe it will help if rbi effectively sells gold to the etfs and sequesters them in its vaults. So if rbi have 660 tons of g...
items.description_html:
Interesting proposal. I believe it will help if rbi effectively sells gold to the etfs and sequesters them in its vaults. So if rbi have 660 tons of gold and etfs want 10 tons, rbi can sell it to them and mark it as such in the rbi vault.

It will be cheaper and then rbi can always purchase the gold back when there is a redemption. This will also reduce total money in the system since rbi sells and takes out money from the system.

Eventually it still has custody of the gold, doesn't have to worry about losing access to gold (it can always buy it back) and etf demand is totally fulfilled and safe.

It will hurt gold vaults to some extent cos we will trust rbi vaults far more than private ones. It will reduce some physical import demand perhaps as etfs own about 120 tons of gold this far but it's growing. Rbi has 660.

My suggestion was that rbi sells gold to jewellers but this does something equivalent and probably better.


Samir Arora: If RBI will import equal amount of gold, how does it ease FX demand.
And if RBI does not import then it will be essentially going short against the public buying.

items.title: RT FIMHAS: Re Please see my detailed response on this matter. There is no accrued interest of the last 6 years and its not cumulative as well YES BANK...
items.description_html:
RT FIMHAS
Re Please see my detailed response on this matter. There is no accrued interest of the last 6 years and its not cumulative as well

YES BANK AT1 VERDICT: ₹8,415 CRORE CASH OUTFLOW? NOT SO FAST!
Several media reports and X handles appear to be confusing the reinstatement of AT1 bonds with an immediate ₹8,415 crore cash repayment obligation. These are fundamentally different concepts

1. AT1 bonds are PERPETUAL, not conventional debt.
They have no contractual maturity or mandatory principal repayment date. Reinstatement of ₹8,415 crore of AT1 instruments does NOT automatically translate into an equivalent cash outflow

2. AT1 coupons are discretionary and NON-CUMULATIVE
Unlike conventional bonds, banks can cancel AT1 coupons subject to regulatory and contractual conditions. Cancelled coupons do not accumulate as arrears

3. Understand Dividend PUSHER vs STOPPER clauses
• Pusher: In conventional perpetual securities, payment of dividends on ordinary shares may trigger an obligation to pay coupons on the perpetual instruments.
• Stopper: If AT1 coupons are cancelled, the bank may be restricted from paying dividends to ordinary shareholders or undertaking discretionary share buybacks

Crucially, under RBI's Basel III AT1 framework, these mechanisms cannot override the bank's discretion to cancel AT1 coupons. YES Bank's actual bond terms govern

4. CET1 impact ≠ immediate liquidity impact.
Reversing the 2020 AT1 write-off could reduce reported CET1 capital, with corresponding recognition of AT1 capital subject to regulatory eligibility. This is a significant capital adequacy issue, but not necessarily a cash drain

5. SMBC’s investment- A strategic investment
SMBC acquired its strategic stake in YES Bank while the AT1 litigation was publicly known. A sophisticated global banking investor would ordinarily assess such a material legal and regulatory risk during due diligence, although its actual conclusions are not public

The Supreme Court judgment is important, but reporting ₹8,415 crore as an immediate cash liability risks misleading investors

The real questions are CET1 treatment, coupon obligations under the Information Memorandum, RBI's regulatory position and implementation of the judgment

AT1 reinstatement ≠ AT1 redemption. Accounting capital ≠ cash flow.
#YESBANK #AT1 #SMBC #Banking #StockMarket
Information only. Not investment advice.

items.description_html:
The order is in. This is a disappointment but it's based on some wording where the government order to reconstruct the bank didn't include writing down at1 bonds but the administrator still did.

But some of this was known, the draft reconstruction included the write down. My feeling is they should have written down equity too but too late now.

The at1 is a terrible instrument I hope doesn't get resurrected with this order.

This means
A) yes bank has a liability of 8400 cr in at1 instruments
B) it has higher capital of 8400 cr but will have to take a loss of 8400 cr as a profit reversal
C) what about the coupons of the past years? That's unknown

Now they will have to see if they will ever buy back on the call date, they can decide not to. Rbi can also lower the interest rate to zero. The owners of these bonds will probably not get back further principal if they do, since they are perpetuals with no maturity.

What we don't know is what happens to the accrued interest all of the last 6 years.

Anyone have the court order? And the original prospectus of the at1 bonds?

Now the share of our crude oil import from Russia has been around more than 30% in the last few years. And four years back, the share was as low as 11%, and before that, it was even lower... NBFC credit growth accelerated to 15.8% y-o-y in August 2026, with retail lending emerging as the primary growth engine. The latest CareEdge Ratings analysis highlights a notable shift in portfolio composition toward asset-backed retail segments.

Key takeaways:
• Retail accounted for 58% of incremental NBFC credit, with its share rising to 43.7% of total outstanding credit.
• Gold loans remained the fastest-growing segment, expanding 69.1% y-o-y, supported by higher collateral values and strong borrower demand.
• Consumer durables financing surged 56.4%, reflecting continued momentum in retail credit demand.
• Industry credit grew a modest 8.4%, with power financing growth easing to 8.3%, indicating a gradual shift away from large-ticket exposures.
• Going forward, funding costs, underwriting discipline, asset quality, and portfolio diversification will remain critical as competitive intensity rises across lending segments.

MIDDLE EAST FLOWS: Not only flows have proven resilient, but over the last few days (particularly since Oct 16), SoH traffic has surged despite Iranian attacks.

Total Middle East crude flows (ex-Iran, including SoH and all the bypass pipelines and routes) are back to >90% of pre-war levels (last seen in late Sept), and even higher if using a short 7-day average. Refined products flows remain significantly below. Caveat: flows are very uneven, with some days of large number of tanker crossings, followed by very quiet days.

Overall, physical Middle East crude oil premia has continued to drop; just the opposite of what has happened to flat prices. The Oman-Dubai differential has fallen to a 3-month low of ~$4 a barrel. The differential was >$30 a barrel in mid-Sept.

items.description_html:
RT Jennifer Griffin
Per @Liz_Friden The U.S. is sending the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit to the Middle East, two U.S. officials confirm to Fox News. The ships will arrive in the Middle East by the end of November, the officials said. These new deployments will add about 10,000 Sailors and Marines to the Middle East.

The USS Roosevelt will be the third aircraft carrier in the Middle East, joining the USS George H.W. Bush which arrived to the region in April, and the USS George Washington which arrived in mid-August to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln. This will provide more options for the U.S. as President Trump is reportedly considering ramping up strikes on Iran after the Midterms. 

The USS Roosevelt departed its home port of San Diego on Sunday and the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit deployed from San Diego on Monday along with the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. The Marine Expeditionary Unit and Amphibious Ready Group typically include about 4,200 Marines and Sailors. The USS Roosevelt carrier strike group includes about 6,000 Sailors.

BREAKING: The 15 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for a record 46.7% of the index’s market value.

By comparison, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, the 15 largest stocks accounted for 27.2% of the S&P 500.

The remaining 485 stocks represent just 53.3% of the S&P 500’s market cap.

This comes as Nvidia, $NVDA, Apple, $AAPL, Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, account for 7.5%, 7.1%, 5.9%, and 5.6%, respectively, or 26.1% combined.

This means just 4 stocks account for more than the next 11 combined.

Furthermore, the combined market cap of the 5 largest stocks now equals that of the bottom 434 stocks in the index, the largest gap on record.

Market concentration is at historic extremes.

The world economy is drowning in debt.

items.description_html:
US electricity prices are skyrocketing.

The average price of US residential electricity has risen +11% since January 2025, to 19.6 cents per kilowatt-hour in August 2026, near an all-time high.

Average prices during the first 8 months of 2026 were +40% higher than in the same period of 2019.

The largest increase in residential electricity prices over this period was in Maine, at +90%, followed by California and New York, at nearly +70%.

This comes as the AI boom is intensifying electricity demand, with data centers requiring enormous amounts of electricity to power thousands of chips and cooling systems.

A 1-gigawatt data center can consume as much electricity as 800,000 homes.

As a result, wholesale electricity prices in areas near significant data center activity surged by as much as +267% between 2020 and 2025.

The AI revolution is driving a surge in electricity demand, and households are increasingly feeling the cost.

items.title: RT Prashant Nair: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in an exclusive interview with Rahul Joshi, spells out Washington's priorities - from trade & tar...
items.description_html:
RT Prashant Nair
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in an exclusive interview with Rahul Joshi, spells out Washington's priorities - from trade & tariffs to energy security, the Quad & the future of India–US relations.

10 points.

1. INDIA–US TRADE DEAL
Rubio says the deal is "incredibly close", with only technical details left to resolve. Expects an agreement in "a matter of weeks, not months."

2. TARIFF RELIEF FOR INDIA
"The purpose of making a deal is to have better rates than what you have now"

3. RELIANCE, VENEZUELA & ENERGY SECURITY
Rubio says his Jamnagar visit will explore how Reliance can help India diversify energy supplies, specifically citing Venezuelan oil & more crude from the Western Hemisphere. Also highlights Reliance's investments in US refining capacity.

4. RUSSIAN OIL & US SANCTIONS
Says Trump exercised a national-security waiver to avoid immediately imposing addl penalties on countries trading with Russia. Did not directly address the contradiction over US purchases of Russian diesel.

5. STRAIT OF HORMUZ
Rubio claims energy and shipping flows through Hormuz are at 80–100% of pre-war levels on any given night.

6. IRAN WAR & DIPLOMACY
"It's tough to make a deal with the Iranian regime." Rubio signals continued extraordinary economic pressure on Tehran, but offers no clear timeline for ending the conflict or ruling out further escalation.

7. QUAD SUMMIT
Rubio says the next Quad Leaders' Summit should take place before the end of 2026, in Manila alongside the ASEAN conference. No specific date or commitment on President Trump's visit to India.

8. QUAD'S STRATEGIC AGENDA
Rubio says the Quad is moving beyond diplomatic meetings towards tangible outcomes. The next leaders' summit should "announce concrete actions", not merely produce another set of declarations.

9. US–PAKISTAN RELATIONS
Argues that continued US engagement could help discourage actions that concern India

10. ANTI-INDIA SENTIMENT IN THE US
"I do not believe, nor have I ever perceived, that anti-Indian sentiment in the United States is widespread or deep." Rubio acknowledges incidents of hatred & discrimination but rejects the suggestion that hostility towards Indians is widespread in America.

@18RahulJoshi @marcorubio

#MarcoRubioOnNews18

items.title: Indonesia sold off 12% today ! Why ? MSCI launched a consultation to reclassify Indonesia from Emerging Market to Standalone Market Background In June...
items.description_html:
Indonesia sold off 12% today !

Why ?
MSCI launched a consultation to reclassify Indonesia from Emerging Market to Standalone Market

Background
In June 2026, MSCI flagged that if progress was not evident - it would consider launching a reclassification consultation - this is now happening.

The Issue
MSCI noted in June that investors had raised significant investability concerns in the Indonesian equity market -

a) opacity in shareholding structures &
b) suspected coordinated trading behavior

Indonesian authorities announced a set of reforms,

a) enhanced disclosure for shareholders owning > 1%
b) more granular investor classification disclosure,
c) a roadmap toward a 15% min free float requirement

However
Market participants emphasized that announcements alone are insufficient; they want clear evidence that these measures are materially improving market governance and functioning, which market participants indicate has not yet been observed broadly

IMPACT
- If the reclassification gets confirmed (final decision expected Jun 2027) & FTSE also follows suit, estimates are for a $10 billion outflow
- $10 billion potential outflow is substantial relative to Indonesia’s BoP

PS: The market is down over 43% year-to-date

items.description_html:
RT Nimesh Shah
HSBC on Bajaj Fin
Buy, TP Rs 1270
BAF’s segment-leading performance continues, with MSME loan growth also likely to revive as move ahead
BAF is likely to find enough levers to offset potential revenue headwinds, and protect its ROA / ROE over FY28/29e
Potential capital raise will be positive for growth, profitability

Nomura on Bajaj Fin
Buy, TP Rs 1270
2Q27 net profit in line with estimate
Loan growth guidance for FY27E revised to 26-27%, with medium-term guidance unchanged at 23-25%
Management expects credit cost run rate in 2H27E to be at par with 1H27’s
Given rising rate environment, management has indicated marginal headwinds on NIMs.
Trim EPS estimates by 2-3% & expect ROA /ROE of 4.2%/19.9% over FY28-29F
Stock currently trades at a 1- year-fwd P/B of 3.4x

JPM on Bajaj Fin
OW TP Rs 1260
Delivered a strong operating performance in 2Q, with key metrics in line with JPMe: NII at Rs 133.3bn (+24% y/y, +6% q/q, in line), PPoP at Rs 107bn (+21% y/y, in line), PAT (post MI) at Rs 62.7bn (+29% y/y, +5% q/q, in line)
Key things that stood out for us in the earnings (more details in paragraphs below):
(i) Growth guidance upgrade to 26-27% , underscoring the strong business momentum across segments,
(ii) continuation of benign asset quality trends across segments with only a transient impact in gold in short tenure product,
(iii) focus on RoA preservation despite the rising risk to NIM from higher funding costs
See BAF as the best-in-class earnings compounder supported by a combination of healthy loan growth, operating leverage gains from ongoing AI initiatives and a strong track record of managing credit costs that should support a 21% earnings CAGR over FY27-29E

CLSA on Bajaj Fin
O-p, TP Rs 1300
2QFY27 PBT was in line with
However, adjusted for a macroeconomic provision of Rs3.4bn, it was 4% above estimate.
It was a strong quarter on all fronts. AUM growth picked up from 24% YoY in 1QFY27 to 26% in 2QFY27 and management raised FY27 growth guidance by 3-4ppt to 26-27%.
BAF benefitted on cost of funds due to interest rate swaps, though it cautioned on margins going forward due to rate hikes.
PPOP came in slightly above estimates.
Asset quality remained strong with the net slippage ratio declining 110bp YoY.
Management clarified that it is raising equity capital for two reasons – strong growth and leverage exceeding 5x.
On insurance guidelines impact, it said it would work to offset it, but did not specify details.

@CNBCTV18News @_RituSingh

items.title: RT Nimesh Shah: Bernstein on HDFC BK O-P, TP Rs 1150 Weak earnings growth trend for HDFC Bank continued in 2Q27 While balance-sheet growth remained he...
items.description_html:
RT Nimesh Shah
Bernstein on HDFC BK
O-P, TP Rs 1150
Weak earnings growth trend for HDFC Bank continued in 2Q27
While balance-sheet growth remained healthy & asset quality stayed resilient, weaker treasury income, & margin pressure weighed on profitability.
As a result, RoA moderated marginally to 1.8% despite continued opex discipline.

JPM on HDFC BK
OW, TP Rs 970
Delivered a steady 2Q27 with NII at Rs 346.2bn (+10% y/y) and PAT at Rs 195.1bn (+5% y/y) coming broadly in line vs JPMe.
Reported NIMs declined by 10bps q/q to 330bps and trailed JPMe on FCNR impact.
HDFCB underscored a positive NIM outlook (neutral to positive going forward) driven by positive impact of a 25bps repo rate hike (70% book is floating with a significant portion linked to repo), along with mix shift towards higher yielding retail and MSME, partly offset by full impact of FCNR (B) in 3Q .
A decline in average LCR to 113% (vs 115% in 1Q, 110-120% target range) does reduce balance-sheet flexibility.
Asset quality remains healthy

GS on HDFC BK
Buy, TP Rs 861
2QFY27 core PPOP growth improve to 13% YoY from 8% in 1Q and was 2% above GSe, aided by continued cost optimization.
Core revenue growth picked up to 10% YoY vs. 7% YoY last quarter.
Loan growth trends were positive, and bank saw improved traction in business banking, unsecured loans, and autos for instance.
NIMs, however, declined by 8bps QoQ, a larger-than-expected contraction vs GSe.

Nomura on HDFC BK
Buy, TP Rs 940
Largely in-line 2QFY27, with core PPOP of INR287bn (+12% y-y / +3% q-q).
NII growth of 3% q-q lagged peers (Axis/ICICI at 5%/6%), reflecting lower FCNR(B) mobilization as a share of deposits (3.3% vs 7%/8% for Axis/ICICI).
Loan and deposit growth were healthy at 16% y-y / 5% q-q and 19% y-y / 5% q-q, respectively, though FCNR(B) inflows contributed ~3pp of q-q deposit growth.
However, LCR moderated to 113% (-2pp q-q) vs largely stable levels of 124%/119% at ICICI/Axis, leaving the bank close to the lower end of its 110-120% operating band.
This could constrain incremental loan growth, making deposit momentum the key swing factor.

Kotak Inst Eqt on HDFC BK
Buy, TP Rs 1050
Reported 5% yoy earnings growth in 2QFY27, broadly in line with operating profit growth.
While NII growth continued to improve, NIM contracted by 10 bps qoq, primarily due to the impact of FCNR deposit mobilization.
As bank navigates a series of leadership transitions, it enters a new phase in its evolution.
A supportive operating environment and attractive valuations reinforce our constructive view, although execution remains the key monitorable.
@CNBCTV18Live @_RituSingh

items.title: RT Nimesh Shah: Kotak Inst Eqt on Axis BK Buy, TP Rs 1600 Delivered a strong 2QFY27, reporting 40% yoy earnings growth, while operating profit increas...
items.description_html:
RT Nimesh Shah
Kotak Inst Eqt on Axis BK
Buy, TP Rs 1600
Delivered a strong 2QFY27, reporting 40% yoy earnings growth, while operating profit increased 6% yoy.
Loan growth remained robust at 23% yoy, although NIM contracted by 10 bps qoq due to the impact of recent FCNR deposit mobilization.
Slippages continue to trend lower, leading to lower credit costs.
While operating environment remains supportive of earnings growth, valuation upside is likely to be constrained as stock now trades close to HDFC Bank’s valuation multiple.

GS on Axis BK
Buy, TP Rs 1600
QFY27 earnings were largely in-line with expectations
Thesis of cyclical inflection in core PPoP growth remains on track
This is being led by improving visibility on NIMs, with retail disbursements remaining strong, the CASA growth run-rate has picked up and the rate cycle is turning
Expect loan growth will remain strong, although moderating from current elevated levels
Key challenge is around fee income, where growth remains muted, but we expect continued cost optimization to partly offset that.
Asset quality trends remain strong, and risk is low amid muted trailing growth in unsecured loans. We expect core PPoP growth to inflect from 10% YoY in 2QFY27 to ~15% YoY in H2-FY27 and 20% CAGR during F27-F29E.

Bernstein on Axis BK
O-P, TP Rs 1600
Delivered a mixed 2Q27 performance, with lower credit costs driving earnings growth despite weaker core trends
Loan growth remained robust and corporate-led, although strong borrowings growth pushed LDR sharply higher to 95%
Stable margins (excluding FCNR impact), a marginal decline in NOI (-1% YoY, -3% QoQ) and a sharp increase in opex weighed on PPoP growth, even as a 52% YoY (-24% QoQ) decline in credit costs supported healthy EPS growth (+37% YoY, -2% QoQ)

JPM on Axis BK
OW, TP Rs 1620
Reported a better-than-expected 2Q with NII rising by 11.8% y/y to Rs 153.7bn (+3% vs JPMe), PAT rising by 38% y/y to Rs 70bn (+3% vs JPMe).
While PPOP at Rs 110.8bn came 5% below JPMe on a miss in non-interest income, which declined by 1% y/y to Rs 65.3bn (-11% vs JPMe) & was more than offset by lower than expected credit costs, which declined by 20bps q/q to 51bps (vs JPMe at 80bps) partly helped by a Rs 9.71bn of recovery from written-off assets.
AQ trends were healthy
Valuations are attractive, as it trades at FY28E P/BV of 1.4x which is at a 31% discount vs ICICI Bank & FY28E PER of 9.6x, underpinning positive view.

CITI on Axis BK
Buy, TP Rs 1620
Headline headwinds—elevated opex (+11% QoQ; 2.18% opex-to-assets) from one-off Labour Code provisioning and FCNR charges, alongside muted mid-single-digit fee growth—masked robust core operational resilience.
While headline NIM contracted 10bps QoQ to 3.36% due to optical FCNR(B) distortions, core margins held firm at 3.47%, further supported by structural tailwinds including a 60% repo-linked book, bulk deposit roll-offs, and liquidity redeployment.
Momentum sustained with loan growth at 19% YoY / 5% QoQ (ex-FCNR), led by Corporate/SME alongside improving Retail disbursements.
Slippages eased to 1.5% (vs. 1.8% QoQ); credit costs moderated sharply to 50bps (vs. 70bps QoQ)
Upgrade loan growth trajectories to 21%/19%/18% for FY27E/28E/29E and modestly trim FY27E credit costs.

UBS on Axis BK
Buy, TP Rs 1670
ICICI reported an all-round beat on reported numbers supported by stronger loan & deposit growth.
PAT of Rs148bn was up 20% YoY and was ahead of estimates.
Loan growth of 12.3% QoQ/30.0% YoY (7.3% QoQ/24.1% YoY ex-FCNR-linked overseas loans) was also well ahead of expectations and peers, though material acceleration was
seen in corporate loans other than continued strength in business banking.
NII/Core PPOP increased 17.7%/21.8% YoY, while fee income grew a healthy 20.1% YoY
NIM declined by 10bps QoQ adjusted for 8bps of tailwind from income tax refund last quarter.
Management expects margins to bottom out in 3Q before recovering in 4Q

RT Nimesh Shah
Bernstein on ICICI BK
O-P, TP Rs 1800
ICICI Bank delivered another standout quarter, reinforcing its position as fastest-growing large private bank.
Loan and deposit growth accelerated sharply, with loan growth driven by broad-based strength across corporate, business banking and retail segments
While NIM moderated during quarter, margin compression was broadly in line with peers (ex-one offs) & strong balance-sheet growth continued to support healthy NII growth
Combined with robust fee income momentum and improving asset-quality trends, this enabled bank to sustain best-in-class operating and earnings growth

JPM on ICICI BK
OW, TP Rs 1800
Delivered a broad-based beat in 2Q with NII at Rs 253.4bn (+18% y/y), coming 2% higher vs JPMe, PPOP at Rs 205.8bn (+19% y/y), coming 7% higher vs JPMe, and PAT at Rs 148.4bn (+20% y/y), coming 11% higher vs JPMe.
Core NII (ex-interest on IT refund) rose by 6% q/q and 18% y/y supported by industry-leading loan growth of 12.3% q/q (+30% y/y, +2.3% vs JPMe).
Reported core NIM (ex-interest on IT refund) declined by 4bps q/q, driven nainly by impact of FCNR (B).
While full impact of FCNR (B) will flow through in 3Q & likely to weigh on NIMs, see tailwinds for NIM expansion in 4Q and FY28 with 57% of loan book linked to repo - now incorporate 50bps of hikes in forecasts including one in Dec’26.

Nomura on ICICI BK
Buy, TP raised to Rs 1740
Delivered strong 2QFY27, led by an NII beat and robust balance sheet growth
Raise FY27F/28F EPS by 3%/7%
NII adjusted for one-offs grew 6% q-q / 18% y-y, 2% above estimate, on loan/deposit growth of 30%/27% y-y.
Core PPOP was in line at INR208bn (+22% y-y / +3% q-q), as lower dividend income following a change in a subsidiary's dividend policy, an accounting effect rather than an operating one, offset the NII beat
Bank mobilized INR1.6tn of FCNR(B) deposits (8% of total deposits), 50% of which were funded by its own loans against these deposits; management expects to deploy this liquidity over next two quarters

GS on ICICI BK
Buy, TP Rs 2025
2QFY27 ahead of our expectations across the board, with loan growth of 24% YoY (2% above GSe), core revenue growth of 18% YoY (2% above), NIM 5bp above GSe, core PPOP 5% above, and lower provisions.
NIM delivery was particularly notable, declining just 10bp QoQ despite one of the strongest FCNR(B) deposit accretions in the system (8% of deposits).
Importantly, bank preserved liquidity at the bottom of interest-rate cycle, with LDR at 85%, providing meaningful headroom for medium-term earnings growth as liquidity is deployed.

UBS on ICICI BK
Buy, TP Rs 1800
Reported an all-round beat on reported numbers supported by stronger loan & deposit growth.
PAT of Rs148bn was up 20% YoY and was ahead of estimates.
Loan growth of 12.3% QoQ/30.0% YoY (7.3% QoQ/24.1% YoY ex-FCNR-linked overseas loans) was also well ahead of expectations and peers, though material acceleration was
seen in corporate loans other than continued strength in business banking.
NII/Core PPOP increased 17.7%/21.8% YoY, while fee income grew a healthy 20.1% YoY
NIM declined by 10bps QoQ adjusted for 8bps of tailwind from income tax refund last quarter.
Management expects margins to bottom out in 3Q before recovering in 4Q

Kotak Inst Eqt on ICICI BK
Buy, TP Rs 1800
Delivered another strong quarter, reporting 20% yoy earnings growth led by a similar increase in operating profit
Bank reported industry-leading loan growth of ~30% yoy.
While NIM declined 20 bps qoq to 4.2%), due to impact of FCNR deposits, bank continued to generate healthy CASA growth and low credit costs (0.2%) thanks to lower slippages (1.2%), resulting in a solid RoE print of 17%
Bank continues to assert its leadership over peers by a comfortable margin, with no evidence that competitors are closing gap yet.

items.title: Neuland Labs is agressively filing CEP'S with the European regulator in the last 6 months , let me contextualise the word agressive : From 2017-2025 =...
items.description_html:
Neuland Labs is agressively filing CEP'S with the European regulator in the last 6 months , let me contextualise the word agressive :

From 2017-2025 = 13 CEP Filings
2026 Total : 23 CEP filings
last 6 months : 8 CEP filings

Now this tells us a lot abou the work happening and also the incremental specialties that neuland is going to be focusing on as well in the years to come, I was also surprised with the rate of filings just in the last 6 months , and recent plant visit and pre poning of peptides comissioning and demand drivers seem to be indicating the right things

Again this is not a quarterly story , but they are positioning themselves for the longer term in the right direction

Also not to get too excited and jump the gun it is important to understand that many are also repeat filings but let me tell you the ones worth focusing on more , now getting into some specifics :

The three filings I would prioritise are Dapagliflozin, Entacapone and Escitalopram Process-IV. They offer the best starting points for investigating market access, process differentiation and potential incremental customer opportunities. Rotigotine is worth a more specialised follow-up, but its commercial attractiveness depends on the formulation and patent landscape.

The strongest confirmed signal is dapagliflozin: Neuland has publicly announced the CEP and highlighted its relative scarcity among Indian suppliers. For the other filings, I would not yet claim an innovator tie-up or material revenue contribution.

Dapagliflozin was developed by Bristol Myers Squibb and AstraZeneca subsequently acquired the relevant rights. AstraZeneca markets it as Forxiga/Farxiga. The European CEP gives Neuland an additional regulatory credential for supplying the API to customers developing or manufacturing suitable products.

Entacapone , The main research question is why Neuland has a 2026 certificate identifier for a specific process/form when an older Entacapone Form-A CEP already exists. A second process can be economically valuable if it improves yield, impurity control, manufacturing costs or supply reliability.

Again this is a starting point for some pharma geeks , but the idea is that there is agression , a lot of it , and it is being validated by filings

If you all like such notes on pharma , little technical and more specific , do let me know in the comments , so I do this for all Indian CDMO'S and API as well

items.description_html:
India's Manufacturing Opportunity ~ China+1 And EU+1 Could Drive The Next Wave Of Industrial Growth

Global manufacturers are gradually diversifying production and sourcing beyond China and Europe.

India is emerging as a potential beneficiary, supported by its engineering capabilities, competitive costs, expanding industrial infrastructure and domestic demand.

Here's what makes this opportunity interesting:

🔹 China's Growth Moderation: China's real GDP growth is projected to slow from 5% in CY2025 to 3.3% by CY2030, alongside an ageing workforce, weaker domestic demand and increasing trade restrictions.

🔹 Europe's Cost Challenges: High energy costs, labour shortages and slower economic growth are encouraging manufacturers, particularly in metals, chemicals, glass and paper, to evaluate alternative production and sourcing destinations.

🔹 China+1 And EU+1 Opportunity: India is attracting interest for new manufacturing capacity, component sourcing and export-oriented operations across industrial equipment, automotive, electronics, renewable energy and power transmission.

🔹 Push Towards High-Value Manufacturing: Initiatives covering semiconductors, electronic components, rare-earth magnets and advanced industrial equipment, alongside PLI schemes across 14 sectors, aim to deepen domestic value addition and technological capabilities.

🔹 Policy And Infrastructure Support: Make in India, the National Manufacturing Mission, industrial corridors, ports and improving logistics infrastructure are strengthening India's manufacturing ecosystem.

🔹 Domestic Demand Advantage: Unlike purely export-dependent manufacturing hubs, India offers a large domestic market across infrastructure, automotive, renewable energy and industrial equipment, supporting capacity utilisation alongside exports.

🔹 Future-Ready Manufacturing: Investments in automation, AI, digital manufacturing and advanced mobility could help Indian manufacturers move into higher-value products and strengthen global competitiveness.

items.title: Swastika Infra IPO whose Financial Health is worth noting Combines rapid growth, healthy financial metrics and improving business quality. Revenue gre...
items.description_html:
Swastika Infra IPO whose Financial Health is worth noting

Combines rapid growth, healthy financial metrics and improving business quality. Revenue grew at ~55% CAGR between FY24 and FY26, while EBITDA margin expanded to ~14%, RoCE stood at ~26% and RoE at ~35%. Despite the sharp scale-up, debtor days remain relatively controlled versus several listed EPC peers.

The key monitor remains cash-flow conversion, as strong historical growth has resulted in higher receivables, retention money and working-capital requirements. However, this needs to be seen alongside the expansion in execution: the order book increased from ~₹684 crore in March 2026 to ₹916.6 crore by July 2026, while of which majority is funded bybnodal agencies like World Bank, providing relatively stronger payment visibility. The company also highlights that projects are largely supported by Central schemes and institutional financiers such as PFC, REC, ADB and the World Bank.

Importantly, Swastika is gradually moving from conventional power-distribution EPC toward more specialised and higher-value segments. It entered power transmission and renewable-energy infrastructure in 2026, while larger project credentials are expected to improve its eligibility for ₹900+ crore tenders, where management indicates competition is relatively lower. This can potentially improve both the quality and scale of the opportunity set over time.

At the IPO price band of ₹175–185, the company is valued at roughly ₹597–631 crore post-issue market capitalisation, translating to approximately 14.4x–15.2x FY26 earnings and ~1.2x FY26 revenue, based on the FY26 PAT of ₹41.4 crore. Against its historical growth, return ratios, funded order-book visibility and transition toward higher-value EPC projects, the valuation appears reasonable, with execution and working-capital conversion remaining the key factors to track.

items.title: RT Dhirendra Kumar: A few weeks ago I wrote that a tool every investor can buy cannot set any investor apart. Why AI investing tools don't give invest...
items.description_html:
RT Dhirendra Kumar
A few weeks ago I wrote that a tool every investor can buy cannot set any investor apart. Why AI investing tools don't give investors an edge: https://vro.in/s229348. The line came from Vineet Nayar's new book, Humans First, Machines Second. His point is plain. AI is powerful and everyone has it. Something everyone has cannot make anyone special.
That left a question I did not answer. If the machine is common, what is uncommon?
I think the machine has taken the middle of the work and left us the two ends. It has not taken the beginning, which is deciding what question to ask. It has not taken the end, which is deciding whether the answer is any good.
Ask an AI to analyse a fund and you will get a competent analysis of that fund. It will not tell you that the reader's real problem is not this fund but whether he should be in this category at all. Knowing that comes from thirty years of reading letters from investors.
The machine will also give you ten sensible options. Picking the one that suits this reader in this market is not calculation. It is judgement, and judgement is mostly the memory of having been wrong before.
Then there is the story. The investor who sold everything in March 2020 did not lack information. He lacked a story strong enough to hold him when the fear came. Nobody gets that story from a prompt. AI can help you invent. It cannot invent.
One more thing. The machine agrees with you. Tell it you like a stock and it will find reasons to like it. What a person needs from an advisor or an editor is the opposite: someone willing to say no.
Nayar says the danger is not smarter machines but people losing faith in what only they can do. In our business, that is the risk worth worrying about.

items.title: RT Gauti Eggertsson 🇺🇦: With Mike Woodford's Nobel Prize, this has been a week of extreme joy at his well-deserved recognition (and Bob Hall's, ...
items.description_html:
RT Gauti Eggertsson 🇺🇦
With Mike Woodford's Nobel Prize, this has been a week of extreme joy at his well-deserved recognition (and Bob Hall's, of course). Yet, I won't deny it, also a week of some self-reflection and personal crisis. You see, he was my main advisor at Princeton. Now, looking at my other advisors, one cannot help but wonder: What value added could I possibly have contributed to my own research agenda, formulated in the early 2000s at Princeton? As it turned out, the coming years would be eventful for my other three advisors: Krugman (Nobel 2008), Sims (Nobel 2011), Bernanke (Nobel 2022). With this sample of three establishing Granger causality (predictive, not causal, whatever the name suggests; Sims himself did much to bring the concept into macroeconomics), I confidently stated the inevitable conclusion in 2022 on Twitter (now X): considerable money could be won in betting markets by placing a bet on Woodford getting the Nobel Prize in the coming years. I am not a betting man, but I hope somebody made money.
Yet, there is a twist to the story. How does one define one's PhD committee? The way I have defined it is the people you worked the most with, who wrote you letters of recommendation when you went on the job market, and who then signed off on your thesis later. At Princeton, there was a rather liberal policy on when the actual formal defense took place. At that time, your main advisor dragged in whoever happened to be around to listen to you talk for 30 minutes or so. I don't remember who was actually around for the formalities, except Mike and, hard to forget, Chris Sims.
Characteristically, Chris sent me an email the night before telling me that he thought Markov perfect equilibrium made no sense, which generated a lively exchange. Those who did not know Chris might have thought this was inconsiderate, as if he were trying to block my defense. It was quite the opposite. Chris was just the quintessential scholar. He was reading the thesis and just wanted to talk about it.
But back to this week's reflections. I would be remiss not to mention that there was another, perhaps unexpected by those familiar with monetary economics, utility player at Princeton during my time. And this utility player actually happened to be one of the people I spoke the most with, for I was closest to him in age, TA'd his grad classes for him and, memorably, a Money and Banking class where he taught the entire class using a microfounded IS-LM model based upon a two-generation OLG model. I still remember the puzzlement on one of the students' faces as he asked me in a TA class: So prices are fixed for ... 30 years? And he DID write a letter for me (bringing the total of this group to five!). So, fellow economists, prepare your bets. Given my research agenda in monetary economics, he may seem to be coming a bit out of left field. Then again, he is one of those economists who could advise anyone on anything. The utility player was none other than the George J. Stigler Distinguished Service Professor in Economics and the College at the University of Chicago: Robert Shimer. He's much younger than the others, so it may take some time. But you heard it here first: Prepare your bets!
PS. Picture taken at a conference in honor of Mark Gertler recently. Paul and Rob added, courtesy of AI, ex post.

items.title: RT Krishna Hegde: Yes Bank dominating headlines post verdict. Few things to note while calculating liability/impact a. Interest on the bonds were at t...
items.description_html:
RT Krishna Hegde
Yes Bank dominating headlines post verdict. Few things to note while calculating liability/impact

a. Interest on the bonds were at the discretion of the bank board. Key condition was bank couldn't pay an equity dividend if they chose not to pay interest on AT1 bonds.
b. Interest on the bonds was non-cumulative. If they decided to skip interest for a year, the bank did not need to pay interest for previous & current year.
c. Yes Bank has not paid an equity dividend since 2020.
d. The AT1 do not have a maturity date. Technically, Yes Bank does not need to pay back the bonds anytime.

items.description_html:
RT Tijori
Saudi Arabia is reducing oil cargoes to European refiners. Oil being cut off has happened to Europe before, Abqaiq (2019) and the 2022 Russia Disruption

At that time Indian refiners who benefitted massively were RIL, MRPL AND CPCL

RIL — the big direct winner. Most of what it makes is transport fuel, and the SEZ refinery is built to export.

MRPL — exports ~40% of its output, and half its slate is diesel + ATF. Exactly what Europe will be short of.

-CPCL is an indirect beneficiary. Products transferred from CPCL to parent IOCL are billed on an import-parity pricing (IPP) basis. When international product benchmarks and cracks increase, CPCL's realized refinery-gate prices rise immediately, boosting standalone GRM and operating cash flows.

items.title: Muthoot Finance holds nearly 200 tonnes of gold as collateral. To put that number in perspective, if Muthoot were ranked alongside countries by centra...
items.description_html:
Muthoot Finance holds nearly 200 tonnes of gold as collateral.

To put that number in perspective, if Muthoot were ranked alongside countries by central bank gold reserves, it would sit at roughly 25th globally.

Singapore: ~200 tonnes
Muthoot Finance: ~200 tonnes
Brazil: ~175 tonnes
Pakistan: ~65 tonnes

In other words, Muthoot has custody of roughly 3× as much gold as Pakistan’s central bank holds in reserves.

Of course, Muthoot doesn’t own this gold—it is pledged by borrowers. But the sheer scale of the collateral sitting in its vaults is remarkable.

The goal: 35-40 products designed and built in India, for rail, defence, mining and future mobility.

items.title: OIL PRICES MAY FALL. BUT INDIA'S NEXT INFLATION SHOCK COULD STILL BE COMING. 🇮🇳 India already ranks 2nd among 8 economies in rubber and plastics...
items.description_html:
OIL PRICES MAY FALL. BUT INDIA'S NEXT INFLATION SHOCK COULD STILL BE COMING.

🇮🇳 India already ranks 2nd among 8 economies in rubber and plastics producer price increases, at around 12 percentage points against a median of just 4.8, according to Morgan Stanley.

Look at where India stands.

Chemicals: 14 ppt versus a median of 12.5.

Rubber and plastics: 12 ppt versus just 4.8.

Basic metals: 6 ppt versus 6.9.

Now look at how these costs could travel through Indian industries.

🔴 High direct exposure

Tyre manufacturers, PVC pipes, flexible plastic packaging, paints and adhesives. Synthetic rubber, polymers, resins and solvents are significant raw materials.

🟠 Moderate exposure through components

Auto ancillaries, air conditioners, refrigerators, electrical appliances and building materials. Higher plastic, rubber and chemical costs could squeeze margins.

🟡 Indirect exposure through packaging and logistics

FMCG, beverages, packaged foods, organised retail and construction. Higher packaging, freight and material costs could gradually reach their P&L.

Here's the surprise.

Even if crude oil falls tomorrow, companies may still be dealing with yesterday's expensive raw materials for months.

The next earnings disappointment may not come from oil companies but from businesses that quietly depend on oil derivatives.
